small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs tuned for M=N=K=4096 fp32 on Ada: try BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 with num_warps=8/num_stages=3, and BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8/num_stages=4. Also try GROUP_M=8 with BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=128 to reduce register pressure if spills occur.
- Transpose B (weight) once at cache-build time to a (K, N) contiguous buffer so the K-dim becomes the inner stride for B loads — this removes strided loads in the hot loop and lets `tl.dot` consume row-major tiles.
- Drop the per-iteration K-tail mask: since K=4096 is divisible by BLOCK_K (32/64), do an unmasked load in the main loop and only mask in a final tail iteration if needed; this shortens the inner loop body.
large_guidance:
- Switch to TF32 `tl.dot` (allow_tf32=True) for the fp32 GEMM — on Ada this is roughly 2× faster than fp32 dot and matches the precision needs of GELU+ReLU here. Combine with a split-K or persistent-tile scheme if occupancy is the bottleneck.
- Pre-transpose the weight matrix to a (K, N) contiguous layout in `_build_cache` so both A and B feed `tl.dot` with contiguous inner strides; this is the single biggest layout win on a 4096³ GEMM.
- Consider a persistent kernel (one program per SM, looping over output tiles) with the BN affine + GELU + ReLU epilogue retained — this amortizes scale/shift loads and improves L2 reuse across tiles in the same column group.
